archived_projects.description: Replace FlagBFMCS satisfies_at with a canonical TaskFrame using truth_at. The current FlagBFMCS completeness theorem uses an internal satisfies_at relation rather than the official truth_at from the semantic layer. Eliminate satisfies_at entirely and construct a canonical TaskFrame directly from FlagBFMCS data, so that the completeness theorem states: consistent S implies existence of a TaskModel and world where truth_at holds for all φ ∈ S. Key architectural requirements: (1) Define canonical world states from CanonicalMCS, (2) Define the duration domain D parametrically (positions within each Flag chain serve as durations), (3) Define the task relation R on world states using CanonicalR, (4) Construct WorldHistory instances from Flags (each Flag yields a history mapping durations to world states), (5) Define the canonical TaskFrame and TaskModel using these components, (6) Prove the truth lemma directly for truth_at rather than satisfies_at, (7) State and prove the completeness theorem using the canonical valid predicate. The existing FlagBFMCS infrastructure (closedFlags, chainFMCS, modal saturation, temporal completeness) provides all the raw material. The work is restructuring it to fit the official TaskFrame/TaskModel/WorldHistory architecture. This supersedes the validity bridge approach in task 997.

archived_projects.description: Rewrite ghr93_case_II in CaseAnalysis.lean for code elegance and GHR93 fidelity. The proof is already correct, sorry-free, and axiom-clean (733 lines). The goal is to replace the tau_left/tau_right sub-game structure with a single restricted tau following GHR93 exactly. This requires resolving the fundamental gap between GHR93's continuous order-type preservation and the Lean formalization's finite-position EF games: same_order_type applies to n+3 positions, so orderings at interior points (p_n, e_n) require those points to be game endpoints — which is exactly what tau_left/tau_right achieve. A solution would require either (a) enriching the EF game framework to support continuous order-type preservation, or (b) finding a way to make the restricted tau's endpoint orderings imply interior-point orderings. Extensive research (7 agents, 3 plan revisions) confirmed the blocker is structural. GHR93 infrastructure theorems (untl_witness_bounded, ghr93_untl_transfer, ghr93_construct_en) are proved and available in CharacteristicFormula.lean and CaseAnalysis.lean. See specs/155_reynolds_pipeline_activation/reports/47_*.md and handoffs/phase-5-blocker-finite-position-games-20260528.md for full analysis.

Add a .claude/rules/ rule enforcing plan compliance for implementation agents. Root cause: lean-implementation-agent invented a theorems-as-interval shortcut for task 107 Phase 1 instead of following the planned Burgess D0 seed construction. The agent definition, skill, and workflow docs tell agents HOW to execute (lean_goal, phase markers, builds) but never say they MUST follow the plan approach. The rule must state: (1) agents MUST implement the plan specified approach, not invent alternatives; (2) if agent believes a simpler approach exists, MUST write a handoff recommending /revise and return partial — never implement the alternative silently; (3) plan task items are binding specifications, not suggestions.

Redesign the FMP filtration for strict temporal semantics. The 2 sorry theorems in Decidability/FMP/TruthPreservation.lean — mcs_all_future_closure (line 263) and mcs_all_past_closure (line 281) — are deprecated because the temporal T-axiom (Gphi -> phi) is NOT valid under strict semantics. filtration_all_future_forward and filtration_all_past_forward depend on them. The FMP module is separate from the main decidability pipeline (decide is sorry-free), but completing it formally proves the finite model property. Resolution options: (A) restrict FMP statement to serial frames where temporal seriality holds, (B) redesign filtration to avoid temporal reflexivity entirely, (C) prove the filtered model satisfies a weaker correctness property sufficient for the FMP theorem. Note: mcs_finite_model_property in FMP.lean does NOT directly use these sorry lemmas, so the impact is localized to filtration_all_future_forward/backward.

Prove succ_cofinal (ChronicleToCountermodel.lean:1885): for any points a < b in the discrete limit domain, there exists n such that succ^[n](a) >= b. This is the root sorry blocking limitDomSubtype_isSuccArchimedean → succ_embed_surjective → cantor_bfmcs_discrete_restricted_tc/fuc → dd_countermodel_chronicle_discrete → bx_completeness. The proof must show the succ orbit of any point is cofinal when all domain MCS contain U(T,bot). Approaches: (a) stage-based argument — each chronicle construction stage adds finitely many points, and succ advances at least one stage, so finitely many iterates reach any target; (b) Z1-based argument — FG(phi)->G(phi) ensures succ orbits have no accumulation points from below; (c) constant-MCS impossibility — show the omega-chain construction cannot produce a constant-MCS gap. Analysis in ChronicleToCountermodel.lean lines 1860-1884 documents the known obstacles. An independent alternative (tasks 154-155, Reynolds pipeline) can also eliminate this sorry by bypassing succ_cofinal entirely. Definition of done: succ_cofinal sorry-free, #print axioms bx_completeness shows no sorryAx, lake build passes.

The goal is to find the mathematically purest construction that works WITH task semantics rather than fighting it. Key constraints: (1) Avoid the distraction of CanonicalR/ExistsTask from standard Kripke semantics - these are NOT relevant to task semantics. (4) Consider algebraic perspectives (ultrafilters, quotient algebras) and category-theoretic perspectives (presheaves, fiber bundles, groupoid structure from converse). (5) The correct solution may not be obvious, but it will be easier than forcing standard approaches onto non-standard semantics. This is the crux of the representation theorem.

completed_projects.description:
Develop a weak/reflexive temporal sub-language for discrete frames where G_w evaluates over the reflexive closure (y >= x) rather than the strict order (y > x). Prove completeness for this sub-language using standard Henkin canonical model methods (no chronicle construction, no IR rule), then transfer completeness to the strict system via model-theoretic argument, bypassing the succ_cofinal gap entirely.

Phase 1: Weak sub-language definition (~100 lines). G_w(phi) := phi AND G(phi), H_w := phi AND H(phi), F_w := phi OR F(phi), P_w := phi OR P(phi). Weak Until/Since with reflexive endpoints.

Phase 2: Weak axiom system (~200 lines). Derive weak axioms in the strict system. G_w(phi)->phi is trivial. Weak Z1 (FG_w(phi)->G_w(phi)) derivable from strict Z1.

Phase 3: Weak Henkin canonical model (~500-800 lines). Standard construction where each point is a distinct MCS. No chronicle, no IR rule, no gap scenario. Constant-MCS structurally impossible.

Phase 4: Z1 + IsSuccArchimedean in the weak model (~200-400 lines). Doets maximum principle (Claim 10) + compression from sum-of-zeta to single zeta (Claims 9-11).

Phase 5: Model-theoretic completeness transfer (~100 lines). IMPORTANT: Expressing strict G in terms of weak operators is impossible (U_w(phi,bot) = phi in weak semantics, so Next is not definable). Instead use model-theoretic argument: if psi is not provable in the strict system, then neg-psi is consistent in the strict system. Since every weak axiom is a strict theorem (G_w = phi AND G), neg-psi is consistent in the weak system. By weak completeness, there exists a weak countermodel. This is also a strict countermodel (same domain, same valuation, reinterpret <= as <). Contrapositive: valid under strict -> provable.

Phase 6: Integration (~100 lines). Wire weak completeness + transfer into existing pipeline.

Phase 7: Close the sorry (~50 lines). Replace the admitted limitDomSubtype_isSuccArchimedean in ChronicleToCountermodel.lean with the Henkin-derived IsSuccArchimedean, making dd_countermodel_chronicle_discrete sorry-free.

completed_projects.description:
Build first-principles FO (first-order) satisfaction infrastructure for monadic structures and close the k-equivalence sorry chain.

The current MonadicSentence type lacks variable binding infrastructure: .forall has no De Bruijn index, .lt has no variable positions, and .atom has no variable argument. This makes it impossible to define eval/satisfies, which leaves k_type_of, ktype_finite, and k_equiv_monotone as sorries. The entire Reynolds Theorem 15 pipeline (doets_lemma_1_4, finite_structures_good, one_class, chronicle_is_good) inherits these sorries through the axiomatized KEquivalenceFramework instance.

Scope:

1. Redesign MonadicSentence with proper variable binding. Options: (a) De Bruijn indices for quantifier binding, (b) two-sorted variable scheme with explicit variable positions for binary lt. The monadic case is simpler than full FO — predicates are unary, the only relation is binary <, and quantification is over a single sort.

2. Implement decidable eval/satisfies. For finite carriers and finite signatures, satisfaction is decidable. Define eval : MonadicStructure sig → Assignment → MonadicSentence sig → Bool with proper variable lookup, quantifier evaluation over Fintype carriers, and lt comparison using the structure order.

3. Close k_type_of from the semantics. Define as the set of sentences of depth ≤ k satisfied by M, converted to a canonical representative (Finset or quotient).

4. Prove ktype_finite: finitely many k-types (bounded by 2^|S_k| where S_k is the finite set of sentences of depth ≤ k over a finite signature).

5. Prove k_equiv_monotone: k-equivalence at depth k implies k-equivalence at depth m ≤ k (subset containment of satisfied sentences).

6. Close the KEquivalenceFramework instance fields (equiv_at, equiv_is_equiv, equiv_monotone, finite_types, sum_preservation) with proofs from the FO semantics, replacing the current sorry-based axioms.

7. Refactor all downstream consumers of MonadicSentence to use the new type. Verify that doets_lemma_1_4, finite_structures_good, one_class, chronicle_is_good, and the Transfer.lean pipeline still compile and that inherited sorries from k_type_of are eliminated.

Definition of done: KEquivalenceFramework instance is sorry-free, k_type_of/ktype_finite/k_equiv_monotone are sorry-free, lake build passes, and chronicle_is_good has strictly fewer sorries than before.

completed_projects.description:
Resolve the mixed-case sorry in bx_completeness: the case where neither box(F-prime-T) (dense) nor box(U(T,bot)) (discrete) is in the MCS.

This is the third and final branch of bx_completeness (Completeness.lean:162-166). Currently dd_countermodel_chronicle_mixed_sorry (ChronicleToCountermodel.lean:3327) is a bare sorry. The dense and discrete cases are handled separately — dense uses Cantor iso to Q, discrete uses chronicle + Reynolds pipeline to Z. The mixed case has some box-accessible worlds that are dense and others that are discrete, which cannot coexist in a single BFMCS with a fixed domain type D.

Research needed to determine the correct approach. Candidates:
1. Product construction: build separate dense and discrete countermodels, combine via disjoint union or product frame
2. Ultraproduct: use Los theorem to combine dense and discrete models
3. BX theorem: derive a contradiction showing the mixed case is inconsistent (i.e., every MCS must be either box-dense or box-discrete)
4. Enriched frames: use a domain type that accommodates both dense and discrete regions (e.g., Q with discrete subsets)
5. Reduction: show that the mixed case reduces to one of the other two cases via modal reasoning

Task 122 research report (01_discrete-bfmcs-research.md Section 4) has preliminary analysis. This task requires dedicated research before planning.

Dependencies: None structurally, but completing the discrete case (tasks 139, 140) first simplifies the landscape — only this sorry would remain in bx_completeness.

completed_projects.description:
Prove Doets 1989 Lemma 1.1 (finitely many formulas up to logical equivalence) and redesign KType with a finite normal form domain, closing ktype_finite and KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types.

The current KType definition uses an infinite domain ({s : MonadicFormula sig 0 // s.quantifier_depth <= k} -> Bool) which makes Fintype impossible. The correct mathematical object (Doets 1987 Chapter 1, Section 1.6-1.7) is the space of n-characteristics: for each quantifier depth k and variable count n, there are finitely many semantically distinct formulas.

Scope:

1. Define nfCount (p : Nat) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat — the number of semantically distinct monadic FO formulas of quantifier depth <= k with n free variables over a signature with p unary predicates and binary <. Following Doets 1987 Definition 1.6.1:
   - Depth 0, n vars: 2^(p*n + n*(n-1)/2) atomic types (one per truth assignment to atoms P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j for i < j)
   - Depth k+1, n vars: 2^(nfCount p k (n+1)) (one per Boolean combination of depth-k formulas with one additional quantified variable)

2. Define NormalForm (sig : MonadicSignature) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) — a finite type of normal form representatives (Doets n-characteristics / Hintikka formulas). This can be Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k n) or a custom inductive. Each normal form at depth 0 is a conjunction of literals over the atomic formulas P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j. Each normal form at depth k+1 specifies, for each depth-k normal form with one extra variable, whether exists-x and forall-x versions hold.

3. Define nf_eval : NormalForm sig k n -> OrderedMonadicStructure sig -> (Fin n -> carrier) -> Prop — the semantic interpretation of each normal form. By structural recursion on the normal form.

4. Prove Doets Lemma 1.1 (the main theorem): for every MonadicFormula sig n with quantifier_depth <= k, there exists a NormalForm sig k n that is semantically equivalent (same truth value in every structure under every assignment). Proof by induction on k:
   - Base case (k=0): every quantifier-free formula is a Boolean combination of atoms; reduce to DNF over the finitely many atomic types.
   - Inductive step (k+1): a depth-(k+1) formula has the form Qx.phi where Q is forall/exists and phi has depth <= k with n+1 variables. By IH, phi is equivalent to a normal form in NormalForm sig k (n+1). The quantifier Qx applied to this normal form yields one of the depth-(k+1) normal forms.

5. Redefine KType sig k := NormalForm sig k 0 -> Bool (or equivalently Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k 0) -> Bool). This is a function from a finite type to Bool, so Fintype (KType sig k) holds by inferInstance.

6. Redefine k_type_of to use the normal form factorization: k_type_of M maps each normal form to whether M satisfies it (via nf_eval).

7. Close ktype_finite: now Fintype (KType sig k) = inferInstance.

8. Close KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types: use Setoid.quotientKerEquivRange + Set.finite_range + Fintype.ofFinite.

9. Delete the old ktype_finite definition (dead code, mathematically impossible as stated).

10. Verify all downstream files compile (IntegerModel, OrderedSum, Transfer).

Definition of done: ktype_finite is sorry-free (or deleted and replaced by inferInstance), KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types is sorry-free, Doets Lemma 1.1 is stated and proved, lake build passes.

Literature: Doets 1987 Completeness and Definability thesis (Chapter 1, Sections 1.6-1.7: n-characteristics, Lemma 1.7.1), Doets 1989 Monadic Pi11 Theories (Lemma 1.1).

completed_projects.description: Prove sum_preservation (NEquivalence.lean:190) and doets_lemma_1_4 (OrderedSum.lean:45): k-equivalence is preserved under ordered sums of monadic structures. This is the sole remaining sorry in the KEquivalenceFramework instance and blocks activation of the Reynolds pipeline. The proof follows Doets 1987 Lemma 1.4 using Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse games: given a k-round EF game on Sigma_I m(i) vs Sigma_I m'(i), the duplicator's winning strategy combines winning strategies on individual components. When the spoiler plays in component i, the duplicator responds using the i-th component strategy (from h_equiv i). When the spoiler switches components, the duplicator uses the order-preservation of the index set I. Also close the carrier_order sorries in the Sigma-type ordered sum construction (lexicographic order on Sigma). Once proved, chronicle_is_good and finite_structures_good become closable, unblocking task 155. completed_projects.description: Investigate whether the finite insertion argument can prove IsSuccArchimedean for the chronicle limit domain, as an alternative to Reynolds model surgery (Lemmas 6-13). The conjecture: between any two points at stage N of the omega-chain, the limit domain has only finitely many additional points. Key observations: (1) each eliminate step adds at most 1 point, (2) each counterexample is processed exactly once via Nat.unpair encoding, (3) the formula closure is FINITE (subformulas of A₀), (4) each interval can generate at most O(2^|formulas|) witnesses across all stages. If true, finite insertions imply the successor chain from any point reaches any other in finitely many steps, giving IsSuccArchimedean directly without model surgery. Research should determine whether the construction can add infinitely many points between two fixed stage-N points across all future stages, or whether the finite formula set bounds the total insertions. Related: task 202 (reynolds_k_equivalence_bypass) which currently uses Reynolds model surgery.

completed_projects.description: Prove tableau correctness theorem connecting decision procedure output to semantic validity. The current validity_decidable theorem in Theories/Bimodal/Metalogic/Decidability/Correctness.lean is trivially Classical.em — it says nothing about the tableau. (3) decide_terminates: the procedure terminates for sufficient fuel (relates to FMP size bound). Without these, sorry-free (tableau) in the README is misleading.

completed_projects.description: Make the dataset generation pipeline resumable after interruption. Currently if run_dataset_generation.sh is interrupted (Ctrl-C, OOM kill, system restart), all progress is lost and the entire multi-hour run must restart from scratch. Implement checkpoint/resume so that: (1) During enumeration, periodically flush generated formulas to a checkpoint file so enumeration can resume from the last checkpoint. (2) During labeling, write labeled records incrementally to the output JSONL (or a partial file) so completed labels survive interruption. (3) On restart, detect partial output and resume from where labeling left off rather than re-enumerating and re-labeling everything. (4) The shell script should detect partial runs and offer to resume or restart. Consider: atomic writes to avoid corrupted partial files, a .progress metadata file tracking enumeration/labeling state, and a --resume flag. This is critical for c9 (2+ hours) and c11 (4+ hours) runs that are easily interrupted by OOM, power loss, or accidental Ctrl-C.

completed_projects.description:
Add a structural, model-independent BracketFormula conjunction to VecEAClosure.lean. The existing `conj_to_bracket_exists` only proves existence (∃ n, ∃ bf, ...) which cannot be used inside the VecEA2 negation closure induction. This task adds:

1. `BracketFormula.conjStruct (bf1 : BracketFormula n1) (bf2 : BracketFormula n2) : BracketFormula (n1 + n2)` -- a concrete combined bracket formula whose n1+n2 witnesses are the n1 witnesses of bf1 followed by the n2 witnesses of bf2. Point types are concatenated. Segment types interleave: for positions in bf1's range, conjoin the corresponding bf1 segment with the overall bf2 trivial segment (top), and vice versa for bf2's range.

2. `BracketFormula.conjStruct_holds` -- if bf1.holds M atomMap z0 z1 and bf2.holds M atomMap z0 z1, then (conjStruct bf1 bf2).holds M atomMap z0 z1. The proof reuses the witness interleaving approach from the n1+1/n2+1 case in the existing `conj_to_bracket_exists`.

3. `VBracketFormula.conj_struct` -- a fixed disjunct-list conjunction of VBracketFormulas: given v1 and v2, returns a VBracketFormula whose disjuncts are all pairwise combinations (conjStruct d1 d2) for d1 in v1.disjuncts, d2 in v2.disjuncts. Prove that if v1.holds and v2.holds then (conj_struct v1 v2).holds.

4. `VVecEA2.conj_struct` -- analogous structural conjunction for VVecEA2, combining endpoint conditions (conj) and brackets (conjStruct). Prove the semantic direction.

These definitions return fixed syntactic objects (not existential witnesses), enabling the VecEA2 negation closure induction in EANegation.lean (Phase 4 of task 305) to produce a concrete VVecEA2 from the three-case decomposition.
